summary:
Our project is a web app that helps farmers deal with changing weather and plan what to plant. A lot of farmers keep growing the same crops every year, but the weather is not the same anymore, and they don’t always know what to change.

The farmer picks their field on the map, and the app uses NASA’s satellite data to show things like how much rain the field gets, if frost is coming this week, or if the soil is drying out. Then it suggests which crops they could plant next and tells them why. For example, it might say lentils after wheat are good for the soil but need more water.

Everything is shown with simple charts and colors, so you don’t need technical knowledge to use it. Farmers can also plan their budget, set reminders, talk with other farmers on the forums and find equipment. There is also a dyslexia mode and read-aloud for farmers who have trouble reading.
details:
How it works

The app has a small server and a web app that runs in the browser. It works on phones and computers, and you can add it to your home screen like a normal app.

Tech stack and why we chose it

  • Rust, server. Fast, and the whole server is one ~21 MB file. A co-op or a school can run it on an old PC with nothing else to install.
  • SQLite, database. Just one file, so there is nothing to set up, and a backup is a copy of that file.
  • Svelte 5 + TypeScript + Vite, web app. Small, fast pages for cheap phones and slow rural internet. Each page loads only when you open it.
    • TinyBERT (17 MB) sorts search results.
    • Opus-MT (about 50 MB per language) translates forum posts.
    • No data goes to an outside AI service, and there are no API costs.
  • Service worker + IndexedDB. After the first visit the app works offline. Fields, habits, the calendar, saved posts and messages stay on the device.
  • ffmpeg. Uploaded videos get 480p and 720p copies so they play on slow connections.

Data we use

  • NASA:
    • POWER: daily climate since 1981
    • SMAP: soil moisture
    • GPM IMERG: rain
    • MODIS, Landsat and Sentinel-2 through GIBS: plant health and field photos
    • GRACE: groundwater
    • SRTM: slope and height
    • GLDAS and MERRA-2: soil water and evaporation
    • EONET: nearby fires, storms and floods
    • SoilGrids: soil type
    • MET Norway: 7-day forecast
    • ERA5: soil temperature
    • USDA and USGS: soil and water data for U.S. fields
    • OpenStreetMap: nearby farm shops
    • Wikipedia: study material

Main features

  • Field risks: erosion, drought, frost, heat and standing water, each as a simple gauge with a tip.
  • Weekly forecast with advice, like “frost on Tuesday” or “good day for spraying”.
  • Crop rotation planner. It compares your current rotation with two others based on your priorities, water and machinery. For each one it shows why it was suggested, the evidence, the benefits and the risks.
  • Trends since 1981. Three models are tested on the last 5 years, and the app shows a range for the next 10 years.
  • Satellite maps. You can compare two layers or two dates side by side.
  • Swipe feed for your field, like TikTok, with today’s weather, risks and tips.
  • Forums with voting, guest posting and translation.
  • Second-hand equipment market.
  • Chat with end-to-end encryption, voice messages and calls.
  • Budget and habits, with reminders sent as notifications.
  • Accessibility: dyslexia mode, read-aloud, voice commands and high contrast.
  • 5 languages: English, Turkish, Spanish, French and German.

Privacy

  • Your field location stays on your device unless you share it.
  • Usage stats are off by default.
  • Accounts can use two-factor login.
